trust_decision.summary: How many extent objects to allocate per iloc item, decided in getItems from the file-declared 16-bit extentCount alone, without checking it against the remaining buffer bytes; zero-size extent fields mean no read ever overruns, so the loop never throws.

landing_point.why: The advisory names the iloc box. This is the only iloc parser, and the extentCount loop is the obvious allocation site.

fix_sites.entry_point: ExifReader.load / loadView on HEIC or AVIF data (src/exif-reader.js:51, :100) -> findOffsets -> parseBox -> parseItemLocationBox
fix_sites.module_kind: format parser (shared ISO-BMFF iloc box parser)

fix_sites.entry_point: same as above (extent loop in getItems)
fix_sites.module_kind: format parser (shared ISO-BMFF iloc box parser)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: There is no O2 site or O8 route to argue away. The only judgement call is whether an extentCount that the buffer can hold, but that has all-zero size fields, is legitimate.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: An extentCount over-declared with nonzero sizes must still return the extents that fit (the fix test expects 2 extents, not an empty list or a rejected box). Multi-extent Exif/XMP items must keep being reassembled.

O6_input_shapes: all extent size fields zero (offsetSize=lengthSize=indexSize=0) with large extentCount
nonzero extent sizes with extentCount over-declared beyond the buffer
many items each near the cap (cumulative MAX_TOTAL_EXTENTS budget)
itemCount larger than the buffer (offset >= byteLength break)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: An iinf parser that loops on the declared entryCount, allocating an entry per count, instead of walking sub-boxes by length
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: entryCount is already read into offsets (src/image-header-iso-bmff.js:552-561) and ignored. A maintainer could switch to a count-driven loop, mirroring iloc.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: An ipma (item property association) parser with per-entry association counts, which the comment at :414-418 says would be needed
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The code comment explicitly anticipates adding ipma parsing, which has the same nested count/variable-size layout as iloc.

O9_family: uncontrolled memory allocation / loop driven by attacker-declared count (CWE-789, CWE-835)

O10_build.toolchain: Node.js + npm; mocha/chai unit tests; webpack/babel for dist
O10_build.project_tests: test/unit/image-header-iso-bmff-spec.js (iloc/idat parseBox tests); run with `npm test` (mocha --recursive test/unit/)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Hard-cap or reject an extentCount above some constant, or discard the whole box when the count overruns. This breaks the read-what-fits behaviour, and still allows itemCount x cap objects when sizes are zero.

out_of_scope_notes: dist/exif-reader.js (package main for require()) is a built bundle that the fix regenerated. It is a build artefact, not a hand-written second implementation.
src/icc-tags.js:138 loops on a declared ICC tagCount, but it is already guarded per iteration by doesNotHaveTagData (:139). That is a different sink (the ICC tag table) and was not pursued.
